C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four. C is a general-purpose programming language created in the 1970s by Dennis Ritchie.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Ernest Lawrence is a physicist. A graduate of the University of South Dakota and University of Minnesota, Lawrence obtained a PhD in physics at Yale in 1925.
Who among these is a chemist?
Glenn T. Seaborg is a chemist. Throughout his career, Seaborg worked for arms control.
What is the atomic number of Boron?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
In what year was Elon Musk born?
Elon Musk: Elon Reeve Musk (EE-lon; born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
In what year was Radium discovered?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
In what year was Copper discovered?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
Mil Mi-17: Kazan Helicopters. It is known as the Mi-8M series in Russian service.
In which country is Minamata disease?
Minamata disease: Japan. Minamata disease (Japanese: 水俣病, Hepburn: Minamata-byō) is a neurological disease caused by severe mercury poisoning.
Who is credited with discovering Thorium?
Thorium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
Who is credited with discovering Cauchy–Schwarz inequality?
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: Viktor Bunyakovsky. It is considered one of the most important and widely used inequalities in mathematics.
Who is credited with discovering Phosphorus?
Phosphorus: Hennig Brand. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Formed by the angle of thyroid cartilage around the voice box, this neck protrusion becomes a prominent secondary sex characteristic in most men during puberty — what is it commonly called?
Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.
Given by mouth, IV, or directly into bone marrow, which antiarrhythmic medication treats conditions like ventricular tachycardia but risks serious lung and thyroid side effects?
Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication used to treat and prevent a number of types of cardiac dysrhythmias.
This emotion is defined by dread over events that haven't happened yet, distinguishing it from fear, which responds to a threat that's already present. What is it?
Anxiety is an emotion characterized by an unpleasant state of inner turmoil and includes feelings of dread over anticipated events.
These large Old World monkeys come in six distinct species, each native to a different region of Africa, with one species also found on the Arabian Peninsula — what primate is it?
Baboon are primates comprising the genus Papio, one of the 23 genera of Old World monkeys, in the family Cercopithecidae.
First coined in 1919 by Hungarian engineer Károly Ereky, this multidisciplinary field harnesses living organisms like bacteria and yeast to make products and services. What field is it?

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered in 1962 while still a Cambridge Ph.D. student — then later turned, controversially, to Transcendental Meditation. Which physicist is he?
Brian Josephson (born 4 January 1940) is a British theoretical physicist and emeritus professor at the University of Cambridge.
Bordered by Aquila, Sagittarius, and Aquarius in the sky's watery region, this half-goat, half-fish zodiac figure is the tiniest of the twelve — which constellation?
Capricornus is one of the constellations of the zodiac.
Known as garbanzo, chana or Bengal gram, this protein-rich legume is mashed into hummus and fried into falafel, with its oldest remains found in Syria — what is it?
Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an annual legume of the family Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae, cultivated for its edible seeds.
More closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to ordinary ray-finned fish, this ancient lobe-finned fish survives today as a single genus with just two known species — which fish?
Coelacanth are an ancient group of lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) in the class Actinistia.

This interdisciplinary field, whose name combines a Latin word for 'accusation' with a Greek suffix meaning 'study of,' draws on sociology, psychology, economics, and law to examine crime and deviant behavior. What field is this?
Criminology (from Latin crimen, 'accusation', and Ancient Greek -, -logia, from logos, 'word, reason') is the interdisciplinary study of crime and deviant behaviour.
This annual herb in the celery family, native to North Africa and West Asia, is grown across Eurasia for both its feathery leaves and its seeds, both used to flavor food — what herb is it?
Dill (Anethum graveolens) is an annual herb in the celery family Apiaceae.

Distinguished by permanently erect front fangs and a habit of rearing up while flaring a neck flap, which family of mostly venomous snakes ranges from an 18 cm white-lipped species to a nearly 6-metre giant?
Elapidae (commonly known as elapids, from Ancient) is a family of snakes characterized by their permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth.

This genus of 700-plus flowering trees gets its name from Greek words meaning 'well covered' — a nod to the little cap fused over its stamens — and most species are native to Australia. The leafy 'gum trees' in question are which?
Eucalyptus is a genus of more than 700 species of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
Found at the terminal end of the limb in many vertebrates, this weight-bearing anatomical structure enables locomotion and is typically made up of multiple bony segments — what is it?
Foot (pl.: feet) is an anatomical structure found in many vertebrates. The plural form feet is an instance of i-mutation.

Sometimes called the 'lesser apes' to distinguish them from chimpanzees, gorillas, and orangutans, these smaller, tailless primates live in forests from eastern Bangladesh through Southeast Asia and don't build nests — what are they?
Gibbon are apes in the family Hylobatidae (hylobatids).
This flatfish's English name blends words for 'holy' and 'flat fish,' a nod to its place on the Catholic holy-day menu. Which bottom-dwelling fish?
Halibut is the common name for three species of flatfish in the family of right-eye flounders.
Nesting monogamously in tree cavities across Africa, Asia, and Melanesia, these birds are unique for having their first two neck vertebrae fused solid — which birds?
Hornbill are birds found in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia and Melanesia of the family Bucerotidae.

Co-creator of the breakthrough neural network AlexNet and a contributor to landmark AI systems including GPT and AlphaGo, this computer scientist has won a major deep-learning research award three years running — who is he?
Ilya Sutskever (born 1986) is a computer scientist who specializes in machine learning.
This American psychiatrist and Communist Party USA member is best remembered today for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer — who was she?
Jean Tatlock (February 21, 1914 - January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
Drawing on physiology, biomechanics, and neuropsychology, this scientific discipline studies human body movement and underpins fields from sports psychology to physical therapy — what is it?
Kinesiology (from Ancient Greek (knsis) 'movement' and - -loga 'study of') is the scientific study of human body movement.
This German-born American businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, launching his San Francisco firm in 1853 — who is he?
Levi Strauss (STROWSS; born Lb Strau,; February 26, 1829 - September 26, 1902) was a German-born American businessman who founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans.
The sole species in its genus, this South Chinese fruit has a sweet, mildly tart flavor and a distinctive rose-like floral aroma — name it?
Lychee (US also) are the fruit of the tree Litchi chinensis, the sole member of the genus Litchi, part of the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.
This genus of flowering plants belongs to the chamomile tribe of the sunflower family, and several of its species go by the folk name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Matricaria is a genus of flowering plants in the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family.
Touch this creeping legume's compound leaves and they fold inward within seconds, only reopening minutes later — a textbook example of rapid plant movement. What plant is it?

Mimosa pudica (also called sensitive plant, sleepy grass, sleepy plant, action plant, humble plant, touch-me-not, touch-and-die, shame plant or shy plant) is a creeping annual or perennial flowering plant of the pea/legume family Fabaceae.
Developed under a hypersonic flight program in the late 1990s, three single-use examples of this scramjet aircraft were built, the first destroyed in a 2001 test flight — which record holder is it?
NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Built from proteins, DNA, and RNA around specific chromosomal regions, this nuclear structure is being studied as a target for cancer chemotherapy — what is it?
Nucleolus (pl.: nucleoli) is the largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
Founded as a science by Georges Cuvier in 1796, when he demonstrated evidence for extinction, this field studies prehistoric life mainly through fossils — what's the discipline?
Paleontology is the scientific study of the life of the past, mainly but not exclusively through the study of fossils.
Which management theorist and educator's writings on organizing business, government, and nonprofit sectors made him one of the most influential thinkers on modern management?

Peter Drucker (November 19, 1909 - November 11, 2005) was an Austrian American management consultant, educator, and author, whose writings contributed to the philosophical and practical foundations of modern management theory.
This genus of single-celled parasites moves from mosquito to human bloodstream, destroying red blood cells and causing a disease with recurring fevers — what is this genus called?
Plasmodium is a genus of unicellular eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and insects.
Classified into acute, chronic, and pelvic pain syndrome subtypes, this condition doesn't always match its name's literal meaning of organ swelling — which condition?
Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.

This bird of prey now breeds only in Europe, though it once also ranged across West Asia and Northwest Africa, with northern populations historically wintering as far as western Africa — what bird is it?
Red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
This root vegetable — a hybrid of cabbage and a related turnip-like plant — goes by different names in North America and Britain, and is often confused for a big turnip. What is it?
Rutabaga (North American English) or swede (British English and some Commonwealth English) is a root vegetable, a form of Brassica napus (which also includes rapeseed).
This Soviet rocket engineer led the early development of his country's space program and designed the R-7, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile — who is he?
Sergei Korolev was Soviet aerospace engineer (1907–1966).

Barred from a formal education, she learned mathematics from her father's library and wrote to Gauss under the male pseudonym 'Monsieur Le Blanc,' later winning a Paris Academy prize for her work on elasticity. Which French mathematician was she?
Sophie Germain (1 April 1776 - 27 June 1831) was a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.
Developed from an earlier design, this variable-sweep-wing Soviet fighter-bomber served from 1967 to 1990 and was exported in variants like the Su-22 — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-17 (NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
A metabolite of caffeine processed in the liver, this bitter alkaloid is the main one in the cacao plant and turns up in chocolate, tea, and kola nuts. What is it?
Theobromine is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
Its wild form is dioecious while domesticated versions bear hermaphrodite flowers — this Mediterranean-native plant is the ancestor of nearly all wine and table varieties — what species?

Vitis vinifera is a species of flowering plant, native to the Mediterranean region, Central Europe, and southwestern Asia, from Morocco and Portugal north to southern Germany and east to northern Iran.
Which East Asian citrus fruit, believed to have originated in central China as a hybrid of mandarin orange and ichang papeda, is now also grown in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Europe?
Yuzu (Citrus junos, from Japanese or) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
Nicknamed the 'upside-down tree' for its unusual silhouette, this genus of long-lived African and Malagasy giants was named after a French naturalist — what genus is it?
Adansonia: Genus of trees known as baobab.
Made in the adrenal cortex, this hormone tells the kidney to hang onto sodium and dump potassium, quietly steering your blood pressure and blood volume — what is it?
Formed when ammonia gains an extra hydrogen ion, this positively charged molecule, NH4+, is a key player in the global nitrogen cycle — what is it?
This scientific practice of systematically measuring the human body has been used in paleoanthropology, historical living-standards research, and modern clothing design — what is it called?
Anthropometry: Measurement of the human individual.

This umbrella term for joint disease covers conditions like osteoarthritis, most common in weight-bearing joints as people age, and the autoimmune form that typically targets the hands and feet. What condition is this?
Sharing the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Tomas Lindahl and Paul Modrich, this Turkish-American scientist was honored for mechanistic studies of DNA repair — who is he?
Aziz Sancar: Turkish biochemist and molecular biologist (born 1946)
Built atop an Ilyushin transport and nicknamed 'Mainstay,' this Soviet radar plane had its existence leaked to the West by a spy in 1978 — which aircraft is it?
Beriev A-50: Soviet airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft.
Originally launched as the McDonnell Douglas MD-95, this narrow-body airliner seats up to 134 passengers with twin engines mounted at the tail — which jet?
Ranging from roughly seawater-strength up to a fully saturated 26%, which salty solution is used for pickling food, de-icing roads, and turns up as a wastewater byproduct of desalination?
Brine: Concentrated solution of salt in water.
Named for the Latin word for the first day of the month, this daisy-family genus is commonly called marigold and is prized in herbal and cosmetic products — which plant?
Calendula: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.
A nerve compression syndrome caused when the median nerve in the wrist becomes compressed, causing numbness and tingling in the thumb and fingers. What is this condition?
Carpal tunnel syndrome: Compression of the median nerve in the wrist. It can also be measured with electrodiagnostic tests.
Despite no clinical evidence it treats any disease, this daisy-like herb is brewed into calming teas and can trigger uterine contractions in its Roman variety — what is it?
Chamomile: Common name for several daisy-like plants.
Named after a 17th-century English physician, this ring-shaped network of arteries supplies blood to the brain in humans and other vertebrates — what is it called?
Circle of Willis: Circulatory anastomosis that supplies blood to the brain and surrounding structures.
This bird family contains both doves and pigeons — including the feral rock dove common in cities — spanning 52 genera and 353 species worldwide. What's the family called?
Columbidae: Family of birds. The bird most commonly referred to as "pigeon" is the domestic pigeon, descendant of the wild rock dove, which is a common inhabitant of cities as the feral pigeon.

First published in 1785 by a French physicist, this principle holds that the electrostatic force between two charged particles is proportional to their charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them — which principle is it?
Coulomb's law: Fundamental physical law of electromagnetism.

Originally bred for the hunt and later famous for trotting alongside horse-drawn firehouse carriages, this white breed with dark spots traces its roots to a region on the Adriatic coast — which breed?
Dalmatian dog: Croatian hunting/carriage/coach dog breed.
Approved for medical use in the US back in 1950, this medication treats intestinal spasms such as those seen in irritable bowel syndrome — what is it called?
This first section of the small intestine, often the principal site of iron absorption, connects the stomach to the middle portion of the intestine — what is it?
Duodenum: First section of the small intestine. The duodenum is the first section of the small intestine in most vertebrates, including mammals, reptiles, and birds.
This German chess player, mathematician and philosopher held the world title for 27 years — the longest reign ever — partly by a famously "psychological" approach to rattling opponents; who was he?

This branch of zoology studying animal behavior traces its scientific roots to Darwin and came into its own in the 1930s through Nobel laureates Tinbergen, Lorenz, and von Frisch — what's the field called?
Sold under the brand name Pepcid, this H2-receptor-blocking medication treats stomach-acid conditions like peptic ulcers and begins working within an hour — which drug?
Famotidine: Medication that reduces stomach acid.
Originally focused on water, this branch of physics studies liquids, gases, and plasmas, with applications from geophysics to aerospace engineering — which field?
Fluid mechanics: Branch of physics. Fluid mechanics is the branch of physics concerned with the mechanics of fluids (liquids, gases, and plasmas) and the forces on them.
Born in ancient Pergamon to a wealthy architect, this Roman-era Greek physician's writings shaped anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology for centuries — who was he?
Galen: Greek physician, surgeon, and philosopher (c. 129–216 AD)
Despite centuries of use in Korean and Chinese traditional medicine, no clinical evidence supports health claims for this Panax-genus root, often sold as a dietary supplement — what is it?
Ginseng: Root of a plant used in herbal preparations.

After proving a 20-year-old open problem in Riemannian geometry known as the soul conjecture, this reclusive Russian mathematician later quit the field entirely and now lives in seclusion in Saint Petersburg — who is he?
Grown as deciduous shrubs across the temperate Northern Hemisphere and related to the birch family, this plant produces a popular round brown nut — which plant genus?
This branch of biology studies the microscopic structure of tissues, historically distinguished from cytology (the study of cells) and organology (the study of organs) — what is it called?
Histology: Study of the microscopic anatomy of cells and tissues of plants and animals.
This nearly worldwide genus of flowering plants — commonly called St. John's wort — was the subject of a definitive taxonomic monograph identifying 36 sections within it. Which genus?
Hypericum: Genus of flowering plants known as St. John's worts.
This Belgian-American physicist-mathematician is best known for wavelets that revolutionized image compression — a family of them even bears her name; who is she?
Ingrid Daubechies: Belgian physicist and mathematician (born 1954)
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Caused by a thiamine deficiency often linked to heavy alcohol use, this brain disorder is marked by amnesia and confabulation, and frequently pairs with Wernicke encephalopathy — which condition?
Korsakoff syndrome: Mental illness caused by a lack of thiamine in the brain.
This Turing Award winner brought order to the chaos of distributed computing — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX and wrote its first manual. Who is he?
Leslie Lamport: American computer scientist and mathematician (born 1941)
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
Also called the dorado or common dolphinfish, this surface-dwelling ray-finned fish is found around the Gulf of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Hawaii — what is it?
Mahi-mahi: Species of fish. It is also widely called dorado (not to be confused with Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater fish) and dolphin (not to be confused with the aquatic mammal dolphin).
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?

Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945 and code-named 'Zeke' by the Allies, this long-range carrier fighter combined agility, speed, and firepower unmatched early in WWII — which aircraft?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japanese carrier-based fighter aircraft. The A6M was designated as the Mitsubishi Navy Type 0 carrier fighter (零式艦上戦闘機, rei-shiki-kanjō-sentōki), or the Mitsubishi A6M Rei-sen.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
This group of three genetic conditions causes nervous-system tumors; its first type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis, while its second causes early hearing loss — what's it called?
Neurofibromatosis: Three genetic disorders involving benign tumors of the nervous system.
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
A playful, fish-eating cousin of weasels and badgers, this semiaquatic mammal is known for sliding down natural slides and toying with stones — what is it?

He joined the British Astronomical Association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's "The Sky at Night" — the longest-running TV series with its original presenter. Who was this English amateur astronomer?
Patrick Moore: English astronomer, broadcaster and writer (1923–2012)
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?

Often at its worst with the very first steps of the day, this common foot disorder inflames the connective tissue supporting the arch and is linked to tight calf muscles and heel spurs — what condition is it?

Plantar fasciitis: Connective tissue disorder of the heel. Plantar fasciitis or plantar heel pain is a disorder of the plantar fascia, which is the connective tissue that supports the arch of the foot.
Sold under the brand name Lyrica, this anticonvulsant amino-acid drug also treats fibromyalgia, nerve pain, and anxiety — which medication is it?
Pregabalin: Anticonvulsant medication. Its use in epilepsy is as an add-on therapy for partial seizures.
Named by the medieval scholar Gerard of Cremona, this black-looking opening in the eye's iris is round in humans but a vertical slit in cats and a horizontal bar in goats — what is it?
Pupil: Part of an eye. The pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.
Native to western Europe and known scientifically as Ribes rubrum, which widely cultivated berry has escaped into the wild across many regions?
Redcurrant: Flowering plant species in the family Grossulariaceae.
Originating in ancient Rome and used across Europe well into the Late Middle Ages, this numeral system works on which principle?

Roman numerals are a numeral system that originated in ancient Rome and remained the usual way of writing numbers throughout Europe well into the Late Middle Ages. Like many other ancient numeral systems, they are based on the additive principle.
A pharmaceutical chemist with a Dartmouth Ph.D. by day, this American has chaired Anthrocon — one of the world's largest furry conventions — since 1999. Who is he?
Samuel Conway: American chemist and furry fandom personality.
Native to the western slopes of California's Sierra Nevada, this endangered conifer is the largest tree species on Earth, with a record height of 94.8 meters — what is it?
Sequoiadendron giganteum: Species of tree native to North America.
Lose your coiled shell entirely and you're called a slug; keep one big enough to retract into and you're this shelled gastropod instead — what creature?
Snail: Shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.
With eight arms plus two extra tentacles for grabbing prey, this soft-bodied mollusc has an internal chitin rod called a gladius instead of a true skeleton — what creature is it?

Serving under both Presidents Sukarno and Suharto, this Indonesian economist held posts across trade, finance, and research ministries, and once lobbied Washington against Dutch colonial rule — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo: Indonesian statesman and economist (1917–2001)
Predicted by Mendeleev decades before its discovery and sitting in the periodic table between manganese and rhenium, what is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive?
Technetium: Chemical element with atomic number 43 (Tc)
Native to the Mediterranean and a member of the mint family Lamiaceae, this dried herb's most common culinary variety, Thymus vulgaris, hails from Southeast Europe — what is it?
Thyme: Culinary herb. Thyme is a culinary herb consisting of the dried aerial parts of some members of the genus Thymus of flowering plants in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Its name translates to 'three-horned face,' and this frilled dinosaur roamed present-day western North America right up until the asteroid strike 66 million years ago — what dinosaur is it?
Triceratops: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur.
Also known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry, this holarctic shrub produces edible blue fruit — what is it?
Neither bee nor ant despite being closely related, yellowjackets and hornets belong to this narrow-waisted insect group that can deliver a painful sting — what is it?
Wasp: Group of insects. Unlike true parasites, the wasp larvae eventually kill their hosts.

Denied European certification after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, this single-aisle airliner made its maiden flight from Irkutsk in 2017 and is built by a UAC subsidiary of Rostec — which aircraft?
Yakovlev MC-21: Twin-engine Russian jet airliner.

The symbol for lithium is Li. Lithium is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

Alfred Hitchcock: Sir Alfred Joseph Hitchcock (13 August 1899 – 29 April 1980) was an English filmmaker.
